data.name: Primary Efficacy Objective
data.text: To demonstrate that 3 mg LY900018 is non-inferior to 1 mg IMG for the proportion of patients achieving treatment success from insulin-induced hypoglycemia using a non-inferiority margin of 10%

data.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Objective
data.text: To compare the safety and tolerability of 3 mg LY900018 with 1 mg IMG

data.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Objective
data.text: To characterize the PK profile of 3 mg LY900018 compared to 1 mg IMG

data.name: Secondary Pharmacodynamic Objective
data.text: To characterize the PD profile of 3 mg LY900018 compared to 1 mg IMG

data.name: Exploratory Anti-glucagon Antibody Objective
data.text: Explore the formation of anti-glucagon antibodies to glucagon

data.name: Exploratory Hypoglycemia Recovery Objective
data.text: To evaluate the recovery from clinical symptoms of hypoglycemia

data.name: Primary Efficacy Endpoint
data.text: The proportion of patients achieving treatment success defined as either an increase in PG to >70 mg/dL or an increase of >20 mg/dL from nadir within 30 minutes after administration of glucagon. The nadir is defined as the minimum PG value at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration.

data.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Endpoint
data.text: SAE, TEAEs (including gastrointestinal, nasal, and non-nasal AEs), vital signs

data.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Endpoint
data.text: PK parameters include AUC, Cmax, Tmax

data.name: Secondary Pharmacodynamic Endpoint
data.text: PD parameters include BGmax and Tmax

data.name: Primary Efficacy Estimand: Non-inferiority of LY900018 vs IMG for Treatment Success
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who undergo controlled insulin-induced hypoglycemia and complete both treatment periods with evaluable primary outcome. Patients are excluded if the lowest PG concentration at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration is ≥70 mg/dL, or if they receive an external measure to raise PG concentration either before glucagon administration or within the first 10 minutes of glucagon administration. (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, restricted to completers with evaluable primary outcome in both periods) Summary measure: Difference in percentage of treatment successes between treatment groups (IMG minus LY900018) with a 2-sided 95% confidence interval derived from the 1-sample mean of paired differences in primary outcome across 2 treatment visits; non-inferiority declared if upper limit of 95% CI is less than the non-inferiority margin of 10%.

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of additional intervention to raise plasma glucose before or within 10 minutes of glucagon administration
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives an external measure (e.g., IV glucose infusion) to raise PG concentration either before glucagon administration or within the first 10 minutes of glucagon administration, rendering the primary outcome non-evaluable

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of IV glucose infusion after glucagon administration to prevent progression to severe hypoglycemia
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose infusion after glucagon administration (beyond the first 10 minutes) to prevent progression to severe hypoglycemia; data collected after IV glucose infusion may be excluded from efficacy analysis

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before completion of both treatment periods
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues the study before completing both treatment periods with evaluable primary outcome for any reason, including adverse events, withdrawal of consent, or investigator decision

intercurrentEvents.name: Non-evaluable primary outcome due to insufficient hypoglycemia induction
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient's lowest PG concentration at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration is ≥70 mg/dL, indicating hypoglycemia was not sufficiently induced, rendering the primary outcome non-evaluable

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single nasal dose by study site personnel versus 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen, Novo Nordisk A/S) administered as a single IM injection by study site personnel in a 2-period crossover design
data.analysisPopulation: Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, restricted to completers with evaluable primary outcome in both periods
data.variableOfInterest: The proportion of patients achieving treatment success defined as either an increase in plasma glucose (PG) to ≥70 mg/dL or an increase of ≥20 mg/dL from PG nadir within 30 minutes after administration of glucagon, without receiving additional treatments to increase PG. The nadir is defined as the minimum PG value at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration.
data.summaryMeasure: Difference in percentage of treatment successes between treatment groups (IMG minus LY900018) with a 2-sided 95% confidence interval derived from the 1-sample mean of paired differences in primary outcome across 2 treatment visits; non-inferiority declared if upper limit of 95% CI is less than the non-inferiority margin of 10%

data.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Estimand: LY900018 vs IMG
data.populationSummary: All enrolled Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who received at least one dose of study treatment, regardless of whether they completed all protocol requirements (Safety Population - all enrolled patients whether or not they completed all protocol requirements) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics including frequency counts, incidence rates, and percentages of patients experiencing SAEs and TEAEs by system organ class and preferred term, summarized by treatment group; nasal/respiratory and anosmia AEs identified using preferred terms and summarized by treatment group.

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation due to adverse event
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues study participation due to an adverse event prior to completing both treatment periods

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of concomitant medications for adverse event management
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives concomitant medications to manage treatment-emergent adverse events such as nausea, vomiting, or allergic reactions during the study period

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of IV glucose infusion or other rescue intervention
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose infusion or other rescue intervention to manage hypoglycemia during the study procedure, which may confound safety assessments

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single nasal dose versus 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen, Novo Nordisk A/S) administered as a single IM injection in a 2-period crossover design
data.analysisPopulation: Safety Population - all enrolled patients whether or not they completed all protocol requirements
data.variableOfInterest: Incidence and severity of serious adverse events (SAEs), treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) including gastrointestinal, nasal, and non-nasal adverse events, and changes in vital signs following single-dose administration
data.summaryMeasure: Descriptive statistics including frequency counts, incidence rates, and percentages of patients experiencing SAEs and TEAEs by system organ class and preferred term, summarized by treatment group; nasal/respiratory and anosmia AEs identified using preferred terms and summarized by treatment group

data.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Estimand: LY900018 vs IMG
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who are randomized and receive at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, with evaluable PK samples collected during the study (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation with evaluable PK data) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, geometric mean, median, minimum, maximum) for PK parameters by treatment group; comparative summary of PK parameters between LY900018 and IMG.

intercurrentEvents.name: Missing or insufficient PK samples
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient has missing, hemolyzed, or otherwise non-evaluable PK blood samples that prevent reliable estimation of one or more PK parameters

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of IV glucose infusion after glucagon administration
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose infusion after glucagon administration to prevent progression to severe hypoglycemia, which may affect glucagon PK measurements

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before completion of PK sampling
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues the study or leaves the clinical research unit before completion of the full 4-hour post-dose PK sampling schedule

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single nasal dose versus 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen, Novo Nordisk A/S) administered as a single IM injection, with serial blood sampling for glucagon concentration immediately before and up to 4 hours following administration
data.analysisPopulation: Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation with evaluable PK data
data.variableOfInterest: Pharmacokinetic parameters derived from glucagon plasma concentration-time profiles including area under the concentration-time curve (AUC), maximum observed concentration (Cmax), and time to maximum concentration (Tmax) following single-dose administration
data.summaryMeasure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, geometric mean, median, minimum, maximum) for PK parameters by treatment group; comparative summary of PK parameters between LY900018 and IMG

data.name: Secondary Pharmacodynamic Estimand: LY900018 vs IMG
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who are randomized and receive at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, with evaluable PD (plasma glucose) samples collected during the study (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation with evaluable PD data) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, geometric mean, median, minimum, maximum) for PD parameters by treatment group; comparative summary of PD parameters between LY900018 and IMG.

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of additional intervention to raise plasma glucose after glucagon administration
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose infusion or other external measure to raise PG concentration after glucagon administration; measurements taken after the time of intervention will be excluded from PD analysis

intercurrentEvents.name: Missing or insufficient PD plasma glucose samples
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient has missing or otherwise non-evaluable plasma glucose samples that prevent reliable estimation of one or more PD parameters

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before completion of PD sampling
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues the study or leaves the clinical research unit before completion of the full post-dose plasma glucose sampling schedule

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single nasal dose versus 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen, Novo Nordisk A/S) administered as a single IM injection, with serial blood sampling for plasma glucose concentration immediately before and up to 4 hours following administration
data.analysisPopulation: Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation with evaluable PD data
data.variableOfInterest: Pharmacodynamic parameters derived from plasma glucose concentration-time profiles including maximum plasma glucose concentration (BGmax) and time to maximum plasma glucose concentration (Tmax) following single-dose glucagon administration
data.summaryMeasure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, geometric mean, median, minimum, maximum) for PD parameters by treatment group; comparative summary of PD parameters between LY900018 and IMG

data.name: Exploratory Anti-glucagon Antibody Estimand
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who are randomized and receive at least one dose of LY900018 or IMG and have evaluable antibody samples collected at baseline and follow-up (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product with evaluable anti-glucagon antibody data) Summary measure: Descriptive summary of the proportion of patients with detectable anti-glucagon antibodies by treatment group; frequency counts and percentages.

intercurrentEvents.name: Missing follow-up antibody sample
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient does not attend the follow-up visit or does not provide an evaluable blood sample for anti-glucagon antibody assessment 26 to 30 days after last study treatment

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before follow-up antibody assessment
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient withdraws consent or is lost to follow-up before the scheduled antibody assessment at the follow-up visit

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single nasal dose versus 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen, Novo Nordisk A/S) administered as a single IM injection, with antibody assessment at follow-up visit 26 to 30 days after last study treatment
data.analysisPopulation: Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product with evaluable anti-glucagon antibody data
data.variableOfInterest: Presence or absence of anti-glucagon antibodies assessed at follow-up visit (26 to 30 days after last study treatment) following single-dose administration of LY900018 or IMG
data.summaryMeasure: Descriptive summary of the proportion of patients with detectable anti-glucagon antibodies by treatment group; frequency counts and percentages

data.name: Exploratory Hypoglycemia Symptoms Recovery Estimand
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who are randomized and receive at least one dose of investigational product and complete the hypoglycemia symptoms questionnaire at baseline and post-dose time points (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product with evaluable hypoglycemia symptom questionnaire data) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, maximum) for baseline, post-dose time point values, and absolute change from baseline in total score and each subscale score of the Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale by treatment group.

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of additional intervention to raise plasma glucose
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose infusion or other external measure to raise PG concentration, which may confound the assessment of hypoglycemia symptom recovery attributable to glucagon treatment

intercurrentEvents.name: Missing or incomplete hypoglycemia symptom questionnaire
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient does not complete or partially completes the hypoglycemia symptoms questionnaire at one or more scheduled post-dose time points

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before completion of symptom assessments
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues the study or leaves the clinical research unit before completing all scheduled hypoglycemia symptom questionnaire assessments

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single nasal dose versus 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen, Novo Nordisk A/S) administered as a single IM injection
data.analysisPopulation: Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product with evaluable hypoglycemia symptom questionnaire data
data.variableOfInterest: Recovery from clinical symptoms of hypoglycemia as assessed by the Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale total score and each subscale score at baseline and various post-dose time points following single-dose glucagon administration
data.summaryMeasure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, maximum) for baseline, post-dose time point values, and absolute change from baseline in total score and each subscale score of the Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale by treatment group
